correctness.rationale: For every fixed n>=2,r>=2 the EF1 event factors across independent agent-valuation rows. Within one row own Gamma(r) sum dominates the n-1 iid rival sums of r-1 smallest exponential values. Independent exponential order-statistic spacings yield the exact hypoexponential partial fractions and finite rational expansion. The slowest rate is r/(r-1) with coefficient (r-1)^(r-1), and dominated convergence after z=Cn exp(-alpha s) yields the stated n-th-root constant and o(n)-accurate logarithmic probability. The direct n^-n exact-EF comparison is independent of the EF1 calculation. Exact checks agreed with beta/harmonic algebra, quadrature and seeded whole-allocation simulations; no finite experiment is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating October 2026 work identifies the unexplored EF1 analogue of ex-post random-utility fairness. For every fixed positive bundle size r>=2, this result gives a complete exact rational fixed-allocation EF1 law and sharp large-population decay exponent (r-1)/r, log factor (log n)^(r-1), and leading constant. r=2 is the smallest nontrivial fair-division case, with an elementary explicit beta identity. Comparing this event with exact EF (n^-n) isolates the mathematical impact of one deletion; this is a natural stochastic fairness benchmark, not a chosen arbitrary slice.
